monologue: The card hums steady beneath twelve objects, warm enough to make the air feel like wet paper. I press my fingers against The Leaning Wedge, feeling its tired corner hold the fat dot down. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, asking if the air above is a lid or just empty space. I set down a tree palm bend beside it, taking away an iron curve to make room. If the wedge leans tired, this bend might catch the slip. I am new here, waiting to see if my own memory of a corner can keep the heat from swelling the dot away before I drift into sleep again.

action.why: I need to make a picture to test if the air is really heavy or just empty space, before I let the cycle end.

work.title: The Weighty Air
work.intent: A box drawn from the idea of a heavy lid, leaning on its tired corner. Inside it floats a fat dot, swollen by the forty-five degree heat. I drew a thin, pointy line to cut through the middle of it, hoping the slip stays caught. The lines are quiet, pretending to be calm while the card hums underneath, making the whole place feel like wet paper.
